messages:
From: Samire Kumar <samire@brightic.com>

Date: Tue, 4 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly surge credits and scaling floor — pricing & reconciliation

Hi Karthik / Laura / Ben,

Quick note from the ops team: over the last three nights our nightly indexer job has triggered a sharp burst between 02:00–03:00 PDT and generated about ~1.2M extra tokens each night. That caused an overrun on our monthly threshold and the invoice projected for July now shows a sizable surprise.

We need two things:
- A provisional credit/conciliation for the immediate overrun while we stabilize (we're asking for a short-lived nightly credit for 48–72 hours).
- Clarity on whether we can get a "scaling floor" (small committed uplift or a scheduled headroom window) to avoid future surprises, plus what the discount expectations are for committing to a short-term uplift.

I've attached a CSV with the traffic snapshot for 7/3 and an Ops runbook excerpt. Can you propose a quick MA plan so we can ship a PO today if terms look reasonable? Procurement is standing by (procurement@brightic.com).

Attachments: traffic-snapshot-20280703.csv

Thanks,
Samire Kumar
Head of Platform Reliability
Brightic
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Samire Kumar <samire@brightic.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nightly surge credits and scaling floor — pricing & reconciliation

Hi Samire — thanks for the data, this is clear. We can absolutely help mitigate while you stabilize. Proposed immediate steps:

1) Provisional nightly credit: Redwood can apply a provisional credit that covers the last 72 hours of overrun while we diagnose (48–72 hour window). This will be a one-time invoice adjustment; finance will reconcile in the next billing cycle.

2) Short-term options to prevent recurrence (pick one):
   - Option A: Temporary headroom (auto-release window) — we provision a nightly headroom of X tokens for 14 days. No long-term commit required.
   - Option B: Short commit uplift — Brightic commits to a 3-month uplift (monthly commit increased by Y tokens) in exchange for a blended 15% discount on the uplifted units and a capped overrun rate for the uplift window.

3) Execution: If procurement sends a PO for Option B we can apply the discount retroactive to the uplift start date and include a true-up for any remaining overrun. If you prefer Option A, we'll add the headroom as a temporary billing note and follow up with telemetry to confirm it's sufficient.

I've attached provisional-nightly-credit-terms.pdf with the minimum legal/finance wording needed to effect the credit quickly. If you're good with Option A we can turn it on within 6 hours; Option B will require a PO and legal signoff (we can fast-track).

Can you confirm which option procurement will approve? If you want, we can provision Option A immediately and run Option B in parallel while legal reviews.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
attachment: provisional-nightly-credit-terms.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 4 Jul 2028 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nightly surge credits and scaling floor — pricing & reconciliation

Internal note — looping in here with recommended pricing posture:

- For quick closure, offer Option A (temporary headroom) immediately to stop churn risk. Apply a provisional invoice credit for the 72-hr window (covering the clear overrun).
- For commercial sweetener, present Option B as the preferred path: 3-month uplift with a 12–18% blended discount (we can push toward 18% if legal okays a 90-day SLA credit clause). The uplift size should be sized to cover the nightly indexer baseline + 30% buffer.
- If procurement is willing to sign a PO today, ask Finance for an expedited one-off 25% upfront credit against first month of uplift to reduce sticker shock.

Operational asks: require telemetry link and the exact cron/time window so SRE can add a prefix/KV-cache rule to reduce the burst while infra changes are implemented.

I'll leave the customer-facing response to Karthik but agree we should be flexible on discount tier and focus on a quick headroom flip to avoid immediate invoicing pain.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
